title: Choose the public site composition
question: Landing statement and published notes share one Kernel page. The roll assigned Issue masthead. Three other challengers wait in the re-roll pool: algorave source floor, mezzotint plate, plankton wake.

options.label: Issue masthead
options.thesis: The public site reads as one dated issue: a named masthead, one statement, then the notes.
options.viewport: Thin ink name, hairline, Newsreader statement at full width, then a flush list of published notes.
options.risk: A masthead can look like a newspaper if the statement does not stay the first readable job.

raised.raise: The first viewport shows the statement and several notes together, never a hero that hides the list.

options.label: Single scroll brief
options.thesis: One reading column: the landing is a letter, the notes continue the same measure.
options.viewport: Centered column: statement, then dated notes stacked in one scroll with no sidebar.
options.risk: Visitors may miss that the notes are a live list if they read as static copy.

options.label: Desk ledger
options.thesis: The public page is the same desk as the workbench: statement on paper, notes in a flush ledger.
materials: cobalt on the single next step
options.viewport: Full-width statement card, then a dense table of published notes with title, date, and excerpt.
options.risk: Can feel like the operator queue leaked onto a public URL.

options.label: Timetable rack
options.lineage: pocket airline timetable as a raked rack of slides
options.thesis: Landing and notes stand as slides in one rack; rank is weight and reversal, not bigger type.
options.viewport: A lateral rack: landing is the first slide, published notes occupy the next cells, a tick rail shows extent.
options.case: Operators already scan queues laterally; the journal becomes a readable rack without a marketing hero.
options.risk: A rake or tinted glass would fight Kernel's square paper; the rack must stay flush and ink/paper.

options.label: Daylight section
options.thesis: The page is one continuous section: the landing is the aperture, notes occupy timed rooms below.
options.viewport: A left section mark, a large landing aperture, then stacked note rooms with dates as occupation stamps.
options.case: Time-ordered notes map cleanly onto occupied rooms; the statement stays the light that enters first.
options.risk: Section language can outrank the journal unless rooms read as notes immediately.

options.label: VU meter bridge
options.thesis: Landing and notes as identical channels you sweep in one row.
options.viewport: A shoulder-to-shoulder row of equal panels: statement, then notes, read by sweeping.
options.case: Fuses poorly: journal visitors do not identify with a recording bridge.
options.kept: The first viewport must show the statement and several notes together, not a hero that hides the list.
options.risk: Meters and red peaks would invent a second identity Kernel does not own.
